meta.description: Things an NPC wants, needs, worries about, or is asking around for.

entries.thread: Looking for anyone who's seen a one-eared cat called Biscuit. Offers a small reward but seems far more emotionally invested than the coin suggests.
Asks if you've heard of a village called Ashwick. When told no, they look relieved and change the subject immediately.
Needs someone to carry a sealed box to the east market. Insists you don't shake it. Winces when you ask what's inside.
Wants to hire someone to sit with them at a tavern and pretend to be their cousin. 'My actual cousin is coming to town and I owe them money.'
Has been trying to sell the same painting for three weeks. Lowers the price every time they're asked what it's of.
Asks if you know anyone who repairs music boxes. Their grandmother's is broken and she won't eat until it plays again.
Desperately looking for a specific spice that their home city used to import. Tears up a little when they describe the smell.
Wants to know if you've ever seen someone walk into the Palegleam and come back different. 'Not wrong, just... different.'
Has a letter they need delivered but keeps changing their mind about whether to send it. The recipient's name is scratched out and rewritten twice.
Is collecting signatures for a petition to rename a local street. Can't fully explain why the current name bothers them so much.
Looking for a reputable translator — has a document in a script they don't recognise. Gets nervous when you suggest taking it to an official.
Wants to borrow forty gold pieces and will absolutely pay it back, and yes they know what they said last time, but this is different.
Has a child's shoe and is trying to find its owner. Has been carrying it for two months. Doesn't explain how they got it.
Needs a character witness at a magistrate's hearing. The charge is 'unreasonable goose.' Does not elaborate.
Insists you try a pastry they made. If you don't pretend it's good, they look devastated. If you say it's good, they immediately ask if you'd like to buy a dozen.
Is trying to track down a former business partner who 'left unexpectedly.' The partner's shop is still intact and the rent is still being paid by someone.
Asks if anyone in the party can cast Detect Magic, then gets cagey about why when pushed.
Wants to know the safest route to Virelle and whether DOL checkpoints are common on the road. Asks very quietly.
Is looking for work teaching — used to teach at an Ars Cultura institution, left abruptly, and won't say why. The subject they taught was history.
Needs someone to return a library book. 'I can't go back there.' Refuses to say what happened.
Has a map that might lead somewhere interesting or might be complete nonsense. Willing to sell it for a reasonable price and one night's hot meal.
Asks if you've met a halfling named Silas. Quickly says it was 'just a name they heard' and won't make eye contact.
Is convinced their neighbour is reporting them to someone, but doesn't know to whom. Watches the street before speaking.
Looking for a healer who doesn't ask too many questions. The wound isn't life-threatening, but they're very specific about the 'no questions' part.
Has a bet going with a friend about whether the Solvetra Vault has a second basement. Willing to pay for credible information.
Wants someone to watch their stall for 'ten minutes' while they step away. It has been four hours.
Asks if you've heard any strange sounds coming from the Echo Veins. Seems relieved if the answer is no, unsettled if it's yes.
Selling a collection of old coins. One of them has a lunar symbol that they clearly haven't noticed, or are pretending not to.
Needs a wedding gift for tomorrow and has nothing. Budget is two silver. Expectations are high.
Is writing a novel and wants to know what it feels like to be in a fight. Follows up every answer with enthusiastic note-taking.
Looking for someone who can identify a plant they found near the Palegleam. The plant is in a jar. It seems to be watching you.
Wants to pay someone to stand outside a building and look intimidating for about an hour. No further context.
Has a debt to Lucien Morvault that they can't pay. Asks if you know anything about the man, how forgiving he is, or whether you know anyone who's escaped one of his contracts.
Is trying to reunite a family heirloom with its original owner, but the original owner died twenty years ago. Now looking for descendants. Has been at this for six years.
Needs someone to test whether a potion is safe. Offers reasonable payment and points out that it's 'probably fine.'
Lost a cart wheel somewhere between Ars Pontaris and Solvetra. Would like help finding it. The cart is still on the road.
Is very interested in the party's recent movements and asks several casual-sounding questions that are actually quite specific. May or may not be a lantern agent.
Has a recurring dream about a door they've never seen and thinks it means something. Looking for someone who interprets dreams. Disappointed by every answer they get.
Wants to hire a bodyguard for a meeting they describe as 'just a friendly chat' in a location they won't specify.
Is attempting to learn a new language entirely from a single poorly-written phrasebook. Practices on strangers. Some of what they say is very rude.
Claims to have seen Myxtiferious — not in dragon form, obviously, one of the founders — in a crowd last week. Looks absolutely certain of it.
Has a locked chest they inherited but no key. The chest isn't magical. The person who owned it was famously paranoid.
Needs help writing a letter of apology to someone. Gets increasingly vague about what the apology is for as you help them.

Is certain that a particular building in Solvetra used to be something else — a temple, they think — but can't find any record of it. The Lorewarden's office told them there was never any such building there.
Wants to know if you've ever been to Kageyama, and whether the stories about Mount Mortifera are true. Seems more hopeful than afraid.
Asks if you've heard the Måneklang. Doesn't explain what that is. If you say yes, they go very still.
Is collecting traveller accounts from anyone who's passed through Lunarthorn recently. Claims it's for a personal journal.
Has a business proposal. The proposal is ambitious, detailed, and hinges on one step that is clearly illegal. They have not noticed this.
Looking for a specific name in a genealogy record that Ars Cultura says doesn't exist. The name is their own grandmother's.
Wants to buy something, anything, from a vendor outside Solvetra — specifically something that didn't pass through a DOL checkpoint. Happy to pay above market rate. Looking over their shoulder.
